correctness.rationale: Direct expansion gives 1-alpha(2-alpha t)S^2/D with t=tr(U^THU), D=sum s_j^2 u_j^TH^{-1}u_j. The marked-frame lemma follows by completing a frame to an orthogonal matrix, taking entrywise squared coordinates and maximizing a linear functional at a Birkhoff permutation vertex, yielding alpha t+J_r u_k^TH^{-1}u_k<=2. Bounding D<=dmax S^2 gives the universal envelope, and eigenframes with singular spectrum (1,epsilon,...,epsilon) give sharpness. All strictness, rank, endpoint and convex minimization claims follow in elementary finite dimensions. A standalone checker passed 56010 exact-rational and randomized reconstruction assertions; finite tests do not replace the complete analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 matrix-quadratic source proves the update identity and the global top-r trace threshold, while Shulgin et al. independently establish the full-rank special case and an uncoupled active-subspace rank bound. The newly proved sharp marked-eigenvalue assignment envelope for genuine intermediate ranks 1<r<d couples the eigenvalue carrying nearly all singular mass with the remaining r-1 selected curvatures. This stronger spectrum-resolved envelope, its strict rank-activation penalty and unique fixed-rank minimax step are not implications of the inspected sufficient bounds. Published research-index queries and prior-claim comparisons revealed no identical/dominating statement; historical bibliographic priority remains a risk.
residual_risks: An older general variational or matrix inequality may subsume the marked-frame optimization, even though no direct primary or indexed comparison was found.
Search index coverage and historical bibliographic coverage are non-exhaustive. Full-rank and rank-one special cases are known, not presented as novel.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 theorem estimates contraction by separately optimizing minimum eigenvalue and active trace, even though these extrema cannot always coincide for intermediate ranks. The coupled marked-frame theorem computes the exact best possible per-rank guarantee from the full Hessian spectrum, with a 0.9168 versus 0.9744 certified comparison on a small natural three-mode anisotropic example and a quantifiable strict rank-activation cost. It supports fixed-step selection for numerical matrix optimization without overclaiming trajectory sharpness. The nonattained extremizers explain why very weak singular components still affect the worst-case polar update.
